card.name: Just before 'men' or a person answer
card.fires_on: Words right before a likely 'men' or a person's name: numbers and 'my' in troop-count text, and the period after a choice letter (a, b) in 'Who...?' quiz questions.

modes.label: Troop counts
modes.description: A number or 'my', 'a few', 'two or three' right before 'men' or 'warriors' in military or historical text.
modes.example: a guard of two or<< three>> men, a private came from the front

modes.label: Quiz answer letters
modes.description: The period after a choice letter in a multiple-choice 'Who' question whose options are people's names.
modes.example: Who did Atticus think killed Bob Ewell? a. Boo Radley b<<.>> Scout c. Jem d. Tom

card.writes: It seems to push toward words for people such as men or villagers, and away from job-title and technical words.
card.plain: It fires where the next word is likely a group of men or a person's name, as in troop counts and 'Who' quiz options.
